references.text: Warning against letting the gods of the nations become a snare for Israel, the same theme of avoiding being trapped by other peoples' religious customs.
Exhortation to guard against making a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, so that they do not become a snare.
Joshua's warning to Israel not to mix with the remaining peoples and not to mention the names of their gods or worship them.
The Lord's warning that the gods of foreign nations would become a snare for Israel, fulfilling the warning in Deuteronomy.
Solomon's heart was turned away to other gods through his foreign wives, an example of what Moses warned against.
The Israelites followed the customs of the nations whom the Lord had driven out, exactly what Moses warned against.
Jeremiah warns against learning the ways of the nations, the same principle of not imitating the religious practices of the peoples.
Ezekiel refers to Israel's desire to be like the nations and serve wood and stone, a direct parallel to the warning in Deuteronomy.
